name: Secularism
summary: Political secularism holds that religion and government should be kept separate: the state recognises and funds no religion, enforces no religious law, protects freedom of conscience and treats believers and non-believers equally. Its strands range from the separationist US model and the strict French laïcité to accommodationist models in which the state supports religion impartially.
scope: Mainstream political secularism as a church-state doctrine, drawing on George Holyoake's English Secularism (1896), the 1905 French separation law and the liberal-democratic literature. It excludes state atheism, which Wikipedia notes may not count as secularism. Most answers outside religion and state are low-confidence inferences.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Strands differ: the French republican model rejects ethnic autonomy while liberal-pluralist secularists accept it; the doctrine itself is silent.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Secularism says nothing on territorial disputes; democratic secularists tend to favour a vote but this is not part of the doctrine.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: A church-state doctrine with no stated view on borders; adherents are split.

simple-living.rationale: Secularism leaves personal ways of life to individual conscience and is neutral on asceticism versus abundance.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred only that its equal-rights stance pulls one way and protection of minorities the other.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from secularism's equal-citizenship principle that obligations should not differ by sex; the sources do not mention conscription.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Secularism is silent on national spiritual attachment; it neither affirms nor rejects it, so the answer is neutral by inference.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the rule of civil law that secularism presupposes; secularist sources say nothing on killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Foreign alignment lies outside church-state doctrine; secularism has no position on China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Secularism has no position on kin minorities abroad; inferred as indifferent.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Secularism takes no position on property in natural resources; inferred as indifferent.

self-ownership.rationale: Freedom of conscience and the equal treatment of individuals fit self-ownership of one's body and mind, though secularism has no economic theory of labour rights; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Taxation is outside the doctrine; secularism has no position.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Welfare design is outside the doctrine; secularism has no position.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Secular liberal-democratic thought accepts parties and civil society as channels of representation, so bypassing them conflicts with it; inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Business policy is outside the doctrine, though equal treatment of citizens loosely favours no privileges; inferred as neutral.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Keeping religion and politics separate is the core of secularism, and organising politics by denomination contradicts it.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Secularism is neutral on tradition but its Enlightenment roots favour modernity over appeals to ancestral religious values; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from secularism's rejection of religious personal law; the statement could also be met or denied by a secular law, which the doctrine does not address.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resource ownership is outside the doctrine; secularism has no position.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Secularism is about religion and state and takes no position on fairness of distribution.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on financial taxation.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Equal treatment regardless of belief suggests concern with discrimination, but this is inferred and adherents differ.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Secularists split between natural-law and positivist views of law; the doctrine does not decide it.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on the world order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on the theory of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Secularism is neutral on patriotism and economic politics; adherents range across the spectrum.

material-over-identity.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on left priorities; adherents differ.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on party-led economies.

missingStatements.text: State schools should not provide religious instruction.
missingStatements.rationale: Holyoake stressed secular instruction in schools and the 1905 French law banned religious instruction in state primary schools.

notes: Accommodationist secularists (India, pillarized states) would answer school-voucher, religious-symbol and personal-law questions differently from strict laïcité. Deepen pass (2026-10-29): searched Holyoake's English Secularism (full text), the 1905 law, laïcité, and the programmes of the NSS and Americans United for the economy, world, ecology, technology, means and globalism themes. Beyond church-state questions they state only opposition to public money for religious schools (vouchers) and the state's neutrality on doctrine; on assisted dying, abortion and same-sex marriage they ask only that religious doctrine not decide, and the NSS says its members differ. Several earlier medium answers deduced from general equality were lowered.
